docs.title: Coyote previs
docs.text:
Coyote is Leal's game; this wiki covers its previs: the shot-by-shot staging of the demo's cinematics in Freya (the in-house previs tool), with storyboards drawn for the START and END frame of each shot and approved by Leal before the shot moves on. The Registry is the canonical list of shot ids, with each shot's approved boards; Help collects how-tos for Freya and the board process, and the registry's own rules.

This is a local wiki. Content lives at G:\My Drive\projects\coyote\ and is shown here as text paths only.

docs.title: How-tos
docs.text:
Written by Adam, accurate as of 2026-10-23.

Rename. Double-click an object or set piece name in the Outliner, or select it and press F2. Type; Enter keeps it, Escape cancels. Ctrl+Z undoes. A name already used, or an empty one, is refused with a log line.

Delete. Select an object, set piece or mark (in the Outliner or the viewport) and press Delete. Ctrl+Z puts it back; for objects there is also "Undo delete".

Colour. Select a set piece or object; in Properties use the Colour swatch. "Grey" removes the colour. Colour is stored linear and shows in the Block and Lit views. Uncoloured things look as they always did.

Start from shot. On a shot with no saved file, the Direct panel shows "Start from shot". Type the shot to copy (for example m05_02_03), pick the file (main or a saved version), press Start, then "Copy into <shot> and save". It copies set pieces, props, marks, camera (static), lights, exposure and cast; it does not copy takes, keyposes, in-betweens or hand keys. The source shot is not changed.

Save as version. In the Direct panel type a version name and press "Save as version". It writes <shot>.freya-previs.<name>.json beside the main file and never overwrites. Open a version with ?version=<file name> in the URL.

Takes as layers. Every take is a layer over the performance (solve + keyposes + in-betweens + hand keys). Each take row has an on/off box, a weight field (0 to 1, default 1) and "+ key" / "- key". Weight keys show as blue diamonds on the take's track and ease between keys. Lower lanes mix over higher ones. Unticked takes are not mixed, whatever their keys say.

Head IK handle. Select "head" in the Outliner. Dragging leans or nods the head on the neck (about 13 cm reach); rotating turns the head. The jaw and eyes follow.

Hips (whole figure) key. Moves and turns the whole figure to where it was keyed, carrying the current pose.

docs.title: Freya scene work
docs.text: Everything is done in the Freya UI. Use Save as version under a new name; main files are never overwritten. A missing control is requested from Adam, never scripted.

docs.title: Sunburst storyboards
docs.text:
From Sam, read from the board sidecars and the registry.

  1. Model and settings. Leonardo GPT Image 2.5 ("Sunburst"), Style None, 16:9, Small 1376x768, quantity 1. Prompt enhance off (it is greyed out when references are attached).
  2. References, in order: the scene's anchor START frame, the anchor END frame, then the canon face sheet, used for her features only, never its drawing style.
  3. Prompt shape: a one-line brief, then labelled blocks: IN FRAME, THE LENS SEES, WHAT HAPPENS, CAMERA (lens, height, distance), LIGHT, set notes, the character's DESIGN, and a closing line excluding text, captions, borders and watermarks. Each reference image's role is stated explicitly.
  4. Process (Leal, 22 Oct): the chairs draw anchors in Sunburst, Leal edits them himself, and only his edited pictures go in.
  5. Approval: only boards Leal approves in his own typed words count. "Good for now" is not approval. Superseded boards stay on disk and are never shown.
  6. Filing: shots\<shot id>\boards\<shot id>_<START|END>_<version>_<date>.jpg plus a .txt sidecar, and a row in the registry's Approved boards table (shot id, side, file, version, date, approved by (quoted), generation id, sha256, was id). A re-approval strikes the old row at its own site and adds a new one. The sha256 is taken from the saved G: file.

docs.title: The Leonardo panel
docs.text:
From Adam, from runs on 22-23 Oct.

  • Click path: app.leonardo.ai, Image tab; Model "GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst"; Style None; Image Dimensions 16:9 with Small (1376x768); Number of generations 1. The image icon left of the prompt opens "Image Reference", then Select Media, where "Upload an image" adds a file. Type the prompt; Generate shows the credit cost beside it.
  • The image-reference trap: the panel can silently keep a leftover image reference (and settings such as the quantity) from an earlier session. It shows as a small thumbnail under the prompt, and its remove X appears only on hover. Before generating, check the thumbnail is the one you intend and that the credit figure on Generate is what one image should cost.
  • The Generate button moves down as the prompt grows, so re-locate it after typing; a click on its old position does nothing.
  • Balance floor: do not spend below the balance floor Leal has set.

docs.title: Kimodo in-betweens
docs.text:
Facts from Sam, plus Adam.

  • Kimodo outputs 30 fps; Freya resamples to 24 fps. 30-joint SOMA skeleton. Clip maximum 10 s.
  • In Freya: keyposes are lifted from the solve. Choose the source frame in the keypose lane's "from" list (or follow the playhead), place the playhead where it should play, then "+ keypose". Select two keyposes and "+ in-between" to make a block; making a block does not generate. Generate it from the in-between controls; the per-keypose checkboxes decide whether the conditioner describes that keypose in the prompt.
  • Each in-between is placed on its keyposes' own floor height, so feet stay on the ground between poses.
  • Time and memory: about 2 to 3.5 minutes and about 16 GB of RAM per new prompt, from earlier runs. Not re-measured on 2026-10-23.
  • Avoid: keys and takes on top can hide a new keypose. A take mixed at weight 1, or a hips (whole figure) key on that frame, covers it. Untick takes or lower their weight while staging.

docs.text: A summary of the rules written in the registry itself (G:\My Drive\projects\coyote\docs\Coyote_shot_id_registry.md). The registry is the authority; where this summary and the registry differ, the registry wins. Section headings are quoted.

docs.title: From "STATUS: THIS IS THE ONE AUTHORITATIVE NUMBERING DOCUMENT (RULED 2026-10-21)"
docs.text:
• The registry is the authority for shot ids. The old-to-new naming table is a derived view, regenerated from it and never edited as a second copy; where the two differ, the registry wins.
  • Update flow: Adam's shot breakdown summary proposes changes as a diff against the registry; Sam applies the diff, then regenerates the table. A change to an existing id still needs an approved table from Leal.
  • "Two rules for a mismatch between this file and the breakdown":
    1. In the registry but absent from the breakdown: a candidate for removal. Do not delete it or reuse its number; it stays listed with the flag NOT IN BREAKDOWN until Leal confirms the cut, then it is marked RETIRED/<ruling> with the breakdown run named.
    2. In the breakdown but absent from the registry: an addition. It takes its place in the cut order, the shots after it renumber, and the previous id of every renumbered shot is noted beside it. Never a letter suffix.

docs.title: From "Rules"
docs.text:
1. Form is beat<scene>_shot<NN>, NN zero-padded from 01.
  2. Path-safe beat ids: 3-base and 3-halluc normalise to beat3base and beat3halluc in a path; the beat sheet keeps its own display labels.
  3. No descriptive ids: a human-readable name belongs in shot.json beside the id, never as the id.
  4. Zero-shot beats (3-base and 4, pure gameplay) get no shot directories.
  5. Shot ids are numbered in cut order. A newly added shot takes its place, the later shots renumber, and every renumbered shot's previous id is noted. The rule covers shot ids and clue ids. (This replaced the earlier never-renumber rule, which is struck in the registry.) Still open for Leal: what a cut shot's number does (retire, or close the gap).

docs.title: From "Approved boards"
docs.text:
• Only boards Leal has approved are listed. "Good for now" is not approval, and neither is a relay that does not quote his words.
  • The sha256 is computed from the saved file, not copied from a report. A hash proves the file is intact, not that it is the current approval, so each row also carries the version, the date and Leal's quoted words.
  • A re-approval strikes the old row at its own site (STRUCK/<ruling>, with his words) and adds the new one; rows are never deleted.
  • Superseded boards stay on disk where they were made and are listed by generation id only, never copied to G: or shown on a page.

docs.title: STATUS: THIS IS THE ONE AUTHORITATIVE NUMBERING DOCUMENT (RULED 2026-10-21)
docs.text:
Leal, 2026-10-21: "Let's make the file numbering the authoritative document, and then subject to update from the summary shot breakdown that Adam produces."

This file is the authority for shot ids. The old-to-new naming table ((internal page)) is a DERIVED VIEW of it, with its status marked at its top: it is regenerated from this file, never edited as a second copy, and where the two differ this file wins. There is no second live copy.

Update flow. Adam's shot breakdown summary proposes changes as a diff against this file: new shots, split shots, removed shots. Sam applies the diff here, then regenerates the table. A change to an EXISTING id still needs an approved table from Leal. STRUCK/leal-renumber-rule-2026-10-21: (the never-renumber rule below) the renumber rule below replaces it. Leal approved the table on 2026-10-21 ("the numbering table is approved"), and on 2026-10-21 typed in this session: "6/6b is final".

Two rules for a mismatch between this file and the breakdown: 1. In this file, absent from the breakdown: the shot is a candidate for removal. Do not delete it and do not reuse its number. Mark it RETIRED/<ruling> here, with the breakdown run named, once Leal confirms the cut. Until then it stays listed with the flag NOT IN BREAKDOWN. 2. In the breakdown, absent from this file: it is an addition. It takes the next free number in its scene, never a letter suffix, wherever it sits in the cut. If the breakdown's order differs from the number order, record the cut order beside the ids; do not renumber to match. STRUCK/leal-renumber-rule-2026-10-21: it takes its place in the cut order, the shots after it renumber, and the previous id of every renumbered shot is noted beside it. Never a letter suffix.

FINAL m05 numbering (run 6b, 2026-10-21; Leal: "6/6b is final"): scene 1: 01 to 05 · scene 2: 01 to 06 · scene 3: 01 to 03 01 to 04 (STRUCK/leal-renumber-rule-2026-10-21: Leal typed "lets go with your recommendation" for the b06 shot) · scene 4: 01 to 14 · scene 5: 01 to 06 · scene 7: 01 to 04 · scene 6: 01 to 06 in cut order. six shots, ids NOT fixed (the 5a package), still open for Leal. docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
1. Form is beat<scene>_shot<NN>, NN zero-padded from 01.
  2. Path-safe beat ids. The beat sheet writes 3-base and 3-halluc with a hyphen the other rows don't have. In a path they normalise to beat3base and beat3halluc. The beat sheet keeps its own display labels; only the identifier changes.
  3. No descriptive ids. beat2b_deglove is a description living in a path component. A human-readable name belongs in shot.json beside the id, never as the id.
  4. Zero-shot beats get no shot directories. Beats 3-base and 4 are pure gameplay with 0s of footage.
  5. Numbers are assigned in story order and do not renumber. If a shot is cut, its number is retired rather than reused; if one is added, it takes the next free number regardless of where it sits in the cut. Renumbering breaks every path that ever referenced the old one. STRUCK/leal-renumber-rule-2026-10-21: Leal, 2026-10-21 11:11, typed in Adam's session: "they must always use proper numbering conventions...so they must renumber shots for newly added shots and note the old numbers". Shot ids are numbered in cut order. A newly added shot takes its place and the later shots renumber; every renumbered shot's previous id is noted. Scope: shot ids only. STRUCK/leal-renumber-rule-2026-10-21: Leal, typed in this session on 2026-10-21: "yes the renumber rules includes clue ids" -- the rule covers shot ids AND clue ids; the NC1a suffix convention is superseded. OPEN for Leal, not decided: what a CUT shot's number does (retire, or close the gap).

docs.title: The crate pass — NO NEW SHOT, but shot01 is restaged
docs.text:
Ruled 2026-10-03 (Sam), routed via Soren. 2b stays 6 shots / 33s. The beat sheet does not move.

Kara's reading that the pass sits inside the existing approach coverage is right, but not at the staging shot01 currently has. The damage has to read in motion — shell burst outward, webbing snapped rather than unclipped, lid torn off its hinges — and that is what rules out "NAIC got here first" with no dialogue. Snapped webbing is a detail. At the scale of a ten-metre approach wide it is simply not resolvable, so the shot would carry the crate and lose the thing the crate is for.

So: the case becomes a large near-foreground element and she crosses behind it without slowing. The crate is big enough in frame for the break to read; she is smaller, further back, and does not alter her line.

This is better than the wide for three reasons beyond legibility:

  • shot01 currently has no foreground layer. This gives it one, and depth.
  • "She passes it without slowing" only reads as a choice if the crate is prominent enough that passing it is one. At distance she isn't ignoring it, she's just walking.
  • The crate and her indifference to it become the same image, which is what Kara is actually after.

One honest cost, flagged rather than buried: a near-foreground prop must survive scrutiny. The case has to be built to a higher standard than a mid-ground dressing piece — the webbing, the hinge tear and the burst direction all get looked at. Same prop count, more prop quality. Worth checking against the shootdown sequence's green chest, since it is the same object twenty minutes later and ruined.

Not restaged to a crouch or an inspection, per Kara — a woman who checks the crate is doing her job, and the scene is about the other thing.

docs.title: A documentation hazard worth fixing, for Kara
docs.text:
The script's change log at :533(d) says she draws the glove off "by the cuff, one slow pull." The script's body at :203 says "finger by finger, unhurried." The body is right and the animation follows it; the change-log line is a stale summary of an earlier version.

NARROWED by Adam, who read :533 before acting and was right to. I overstated this. The paragraph immediately after 13(d) is an explicit CORRECTION block in bold, recording that Leal reversed an earlier "deliberately NOT finger by finger" reading, and saying the dead rationale is kept "only so that nobody rediscovers it and 'fixes' the script back down to a wrist action." Kara anticipated this failure mode and wrote the guard.

What remains is real but smaller: the stale phrase sits inside 13(d) and the correction is a separate paragraph a reader can skip. The fix is striking the phrase in 13(d), not adding a warning — the warning already exists. Kara's call. Worth telling her the guard worked rather than that the document is broken.

This ordering is committed for the purpose of fixing identifiers. The full 2b shot list — lenses, staging, coverage, performance notes — is a separate deliverable and does not change these numbers when it lands, by rule 5.

docs.title: Tier is a scene-level column; the Tier 1 requirement is shot-level
docs.text:
Adam's shot.json proposal to carry tier and discharges_tier_requirement as separate fields is correct, and the reason is sharper than bookkeeping.

The beat sheet assigns tier per beat. GDD §12.4 defines tier per shot — "close-up emotion; facial/emotional performance shots." Those are different grains, and 2b is exactly where they come apart:

  • Scene 2b is Tier 1 because it contains facial performance — shot03 and shot06.
  • beat2b_shot04, the deglove, does not discharge the Tier 1 requirement. Not because of framing — I argued its camera must hold her face, and it should — but because there is no facial performance in it to hold. The torso, head and legs are bit-identical across all 168 frames; Leal ruled previs is hands-only and the generative step carries the performance. A face in frame doing nothing is not a facial-performance shot.

So beat2b_shot04 is a capability proof — it answers the finger-animation gap, which is Leal's stated reason for running it first, and that gap does block everything. It is not the Tier 1 shot GDD §12.4:382 requires as a deliverable, and the requirement stays open against a named facial-performance shot — beat2b_shot03 on current reading.

Collapsing those two fields is precisely the failure §12.4:382 pre-registers: a demo that "would look like it validated the thesis while leaving the highest-risk category completely untested."

One consequence worth carrying forward: beat2b_shot04's own legibility depends on performance the previs layer cannot supply. I argued the face must be in frame because the deglove is where she decides — and the decision will be carried entirely by the generative step, against no previs reference for the face. That makes it a harder shot than its hands-only previs suggests, and it is an argument for beat2b_shot03 being proven early rather than late.
